title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is witnessing a mix of advancements and challenges, with new contracts and technologies emerging alongside regulatory hurdles. As the U.S. government increases its budget for space resilience, Europe’s smallsat sector struggles to gain traction.

themes.title: DARPA's Rocket Propellant Push
themes.body: Voyager's recent DARPA contract for solid rocket propellant technology signals a continued interest in enhancing propulsion capabilities. This could bolster U.S. defense capabilities, but the path to practical application remains complex.

themes.title: Europe's Small Satellite Struggles
themes.body: Regulatory barriers and limited access to capital are stifling growth in Europe's smallsat industry, which could hinder its competitive edge. Without a concerted effort to streamline these issues, the region risks falling behind in the burgeoning space economy.

themes.title: Chinese Advances in Rocket Tech
themes.body: Mega Engine's progress on a reusable staged-combustion rocket engine highlights China's ambitions in the space race. This development could shift the balance of power, particularly if it leads to more cost-effective launch options.

themes.title: Space Force Budget Boost
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup adds $1.4 billion to the space resilience line, reflecting a growing recognition of the importance of space security. This funding could catalyze innovations and partnerships in the defense sector, particularly as threats evolve.
